text:
jamal: Heads-up — spotted a spike in evictions on our europe-west pools this morning. Wondering if we should standardize a runtime pattern for preemptible/spot drains (graceful drain + requeue + streaming cutover). Anyone already have a playbook?

liam: We have bits in two places: node-level drain on eviction signal, and a per-request router that can requeue to fallback pools. But behavior is inconsistent across models when streaming.

sofia: Problem we keep hitting: long token streams get cut mid-output and clients see incomplete JSON blobs. We need a deterministic cutover so callers either get the remainder or a clear partial + retry token.

priya: Agreed. Proposal: on termination notice -> 1) mark node DRAINING in service registry 2) stop accepting new requests 3) for active streaming requests, trigger a 'cutover mode' that switches to buffered finalization and emits a trailer event with retry hints 4) requeue short requests to mixed-capacity fallback pool (on-demand or different spot market).

alex: +1. A few nitty gritty: detection sources differ by cloud: GCE metadata 2-minute preemptible notice, AWS Spot termination (two-minute), Azure VM evict (30s). We should centralize a small eviction daemon that normalizes signals into a single internal webhook.

infra-bot: eviction-daemon: registered new watch on metadata endpoints for gce/aws/azure. will emit EVictionNotice events to /internal/eviction.

liam: For streaming cutover I sketched a small sequence: when EVictionNotice received: set request.routing_state = DRAINING, set response.mode = BUFFER_AND_CLOSE, attach header X-Stream-Cut: true + cut_uid. Implementation sketch:
```
on_eviction(node):
  node.set_state('DRAINING')
  stop_accepting_new_requests()
  for req in node.active_requests:
    if req.remaining_tokens < STREAM_THRESHOLD:
      let fallback = find_fallback(req);
      requeue(req, fallback)
    else:
      req.switch_to_buffer_and_close(cut_uid)
      // flush partial tokens, emit trailer with retry id
````

sofia: Two important pieces: a) runtime needs a consistent partial-output format so the client lib can detect and replay, b) KV cache for model must be checkpointable or able to rebuild quickly if requeued (we may need to snapshot small prefix cache or warm target replica).

priya: On cost/efficiency: mixed-capacity pools are great but requeues increase p95 and double-token cost for re-run requests. We should prefer quick local finalization over requeue for large streaming responses, and requeue short requests (< 2s) first. Let's add a cost heuristic.

jamal: Good point. Suggest thresholds: short < 2s -> requeue; medium 2-8s -> attempt local finish with buffer; long >8s -> cut and emit retry header + best-effort checkpoint (KV snapshot of last N tokens). We can tune after rollout.

alex: Also add routing fallback rules: prefer same-region on-demand first, then cross-region if latency SLO allows. Mark requests with "can_cross_region": true/false at API level so Enterprise customers can opt out.

sofia: Telemetry: emit metrics on eviction_count, requeue_count, streamed_cut_count, partial_retry_success. Instrument the client SDK to automatically retry if it sees the trailer with retry-id.

liam: For testing: canary the change by enabling for a small fraction of nodes and run chaos monkey preemptions with synthetic streaming workloads. Measure p99 tail latencies and token duplication.

priya: Example of metadata polling snippet (GCE):
```bash
# poll once per second, stop when termination-time exists
curl -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" --silent "http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/preempted"
```
And for AWS: check IMDS for spot instance action. We'll wrap both in eviction-daemon.

jamal: Next steps: liam implement eviction-daemon + router hooks, sofia implement streaming buffer/trailer and client SDK retry behavior, priya add cost-heuristic config and rollout plan. I'll own canary + chaos testing. Plan to sync tomorrow at noon.

alex: I'll add an RFC with sequence diagrams and required schema for trailer/retry headers.

infra-bot: action_created: [liam] implement_eviction_daemon, [sofia] streaming_cutover, [priya] cost_heuristic, [jamal] chaos_canary. Due: 1 week.

jamal: Thanks — appreciate the quick alignment. If anyone sees a major edge-case (e.g., large multi-turn chat with function-calls) drop it here and we'll add to RFC.
